prs.title: fix(bindings): carry the relay's `stored` flag past the burst's first frame
prs.body:
Review follow-ups on #442. The mailbox park itself was right; what was wrong is
how much of a burst it reached, and a handful of places where the reasoning was
either overstated or not written down.

**The React Native bridges only carried `stored` for the first frame of a burst.**

The relay answers every `SendMessage` separately, but `handleRecipientUnreachable`
reported only what `drainRecipient` returned — and the first verdict to arrive for
a recipient drains that recipient's whole in-flight queue. So with frames A, B and
C in flight to a sleeping peer, `DeliveryError { A, stored }` resolved all three:
A took `relay_stored`, B and C took `recipient_unreachable` and a probe. The
verdicts naming B and C then found nothing to drain and reported nothing at all,
so each of them paid a probe rung — one relay write and one
`MessageUndeliverable` — before the relay said `stored` again and the frame
finally parked probe-free. Nothing was stranded, but on mobile the feature only
really took effect for one frame per burst, which is the traffic it exists to
remove.

The Python client never had the gap: it appends the echoed id when the drain
missed it. Both bridges now do the same, guarded on the id not already being in
the drain so a frame still in flight is reported once rather than twice. It is
safe for an id that is not ours, because the core ignores an id with no outbox
entry, and safe for one that is already parked, because `park_unreachable_dm`
clears the retry slot before it decides whether to re-arm it — which is what
actually retires the probe on the second verdict.

**Tests for the path the fix stands on**

- `test_relay_stored_verdict_drops_an_existing_probe` (core) — a `relay_stored`
  verdict for a frame that is *already* being probed retires that probe. This is
  the ordering the bridge fix depends on and nothing pinned it; without it the
  bridges could report the right token and change nothing.
- `test_a_later_verdict_still_reports_its_own_frame_as_held` (Python) — the burst
  sequence end to end: the first verdict resolves both frames, the second still
  reports its own frame as held. This documents the contract the bridges were
  violating, on the client that already satisfied it.
- `react_native_relay_parks_a_stored_delivery_error` (uniffi source guard) — now
  also pins the append and its not-already-drained guard, per platform. The guard
  as written asserted token *selection* only, so it would not have caught this.
- `test_stored_without_pushed_parks_nothing` (Python) — `MessageSent
  { pushed: false, stored: true }` is an accepted delivery to a live session, so
  there is no park to make and no probe to drop. Every client already gates the
  park on `pushed`; nothing said so.

**Two things the rationale claimed, or left out**

`park_unreachable_dm`'s comment and the changelog both said recovery was "the
reachability edge behind it for a copy that is evicted or expires." The edge is
not conditional on eviction: it fires on any reconnect, and
`flush_outbox_for_peer_via` selects on "in the outbox, not awaiting an ACK", so a
returning peer re-drives a held frame alongside the relay's own drain exactly as
it would an unheld one. What the flag actually saves is the 15s→600s ladder
*while the peer is away*. Both now say that, and both now name the consequence:
past the mailbox's own retention the guarantee is that edge and the outbox
lifetime, which is the same trade `edge_driven_unreachable_dm` opts into for
every parked frame, taken unconditionally here because the mailbox is already
committed to the redelivery.

The comment also now records why `stored` is deliberately *not* persisted on the
outbox entry, unlike `relay_pushed`. A restart re-drives the outbox and the relay
answers `stored` again for a frame it still holds, so the park is re-derived;
`relay_pushed` has to survive because it suppresses an app-facing event no later
answer restates. Persisting this one would also be wrong on its own terms — it
records what the mailbox held at park time, and the mailbox can evict before the
next launch, so a restored flag would suppress the probe on the strength of a
copy that may be gone.

**The gateway contract documented neither flag**

`docs/spec/gateway-contract.md` is the shared spec, and its Submit/Verdict shapes
never mentioned `pushed` (which predates #442) or `stored`. Both are now in the
shapes and in prose: optional, defaulting to `false` when absent, with a missing
key read as `false` and never as unknown. It also states the rule the bridge bug
came out of — both flags are statements about the one frame the verdict names,
never about the recipient — and the obligation that follows for a gateway holding
several frames: set `stored` on each frame's own verdict.

**Deliberately not in this PR**

- A `stored` field on `MessageUndeliverable`, so an app could tell "held, will be
  delivered" from "lost, being probed". The reason string must stay normalized at
  the boundary, so this needs a real field, which touches the telemetry wire
  crate, the scrubber, the React Native event types and `UPGRADING.md`. Its own
  change.
- A Welcome the mailbox holds still runs its own probe ladder. The argument for
  dropping it is identical to the DM case, but the Welcome lifecycle is a
  separate state machine and #442 deliberately left it alone.
- Extracting the id/token selection into a testable policy object per platform,
  the way `PresenceWatchPolicy` and `GatewayVerdictTracker` are. It would let the
  source guard shrink to nothing. Not worth refactoring shipping bridge code on
  two platforms in the same change as the fix.

**Verification**

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean. `cargo test -p offline-protocol --lib` and
`cargo test -p offline-protocol-uniffi --lib` pass, including the three new and
extended tests. The full Python suite passes locally (269 tests) including the two
new ones. The Kotlin expression added to the Android bridge was compiled and
exercised standalone over all four of its branches, since `InternetManager` itself
has no local unit-test seam; CI's Android and iOS jobs cover the real builds.
